title: Vitryne format v1: garments/<id>.json
description: One garment: its pattern pieces (2D, mm), how many times each is cut, where each cut starts around the avatar, and which runs of outline are sewn together.

fabric.description: The fabric of every cut that doesn't name its own.

appearance.description: The appearance (colour) of every cut that doesn't name its own. Absent: the app's own.

pieces.description: Empty in a garment started from scratch, before its first piece is drawn.

stack.description: Every cut of the garment once, closest to the body first. Where cuts overlap on the body, the one higher in the list starts further out. A cut that goes on another (follow) comes after it.

simulation.description: Overrides of the project's simulation settings for this garment.

engine.description: Sparse engine tuning, merged over the project's (same rules: engine keys and units).

collisionBounds.description: The box (mm, avatar space) the cloth can reach, for the body's collision field. Optional: the engine derives one when absent.

sources.description: Imported originals this garment was made from (e.g. a DXF-AAMA file), kept as parts with role source. For reference and re-import only: nothing is read from them.

piece.description: A pattern piece as drafted, in its own 2D frame (mm, +y towards the top of the garment), seen from the right side of the fabric. Cut-on-fold pieces are stored unfolded, with the fold kept in folds.

outline.description: The sewing line, a closed loop of nodes in counter-clockwise order. Each node's edge runs to the next node (the last one's back to the first).

lines.description: Internal lines (pocket placement, darts, stitching lines): open paths inside the piece. They are meshed as creases and can be sewn.

folds.description: Fold lines of a cut-on-fold piece: the straight line between two outline nodes the piece was mirrored about.

grain.description: The grain line, as drawn: its direction (to - from) is the fabric's warp. Absent: +y.

cuts.description: How many times the piece is cut, and how each copy is used. Seams and placement refer to cuts.

source.description: The piece in an imported source this was made from.

piece.description: The piece's name in the source.

node.description: A point of a piece that other things refer to. corner: the outline turns here. notch: an alignment notch. point: anything else worth naming (fold ends, where an internal line meets the outline, a point added for a seam).

edge.description: The path from this node to the next one: a polyline (core) or a cubic Bézier (extension VTRY_curves). Other curve types (arcs) may be added by later versions or extensions.

polylineEdge.description: The points strictly between the two nodes, in order (empty for a straight edge).

cubicEdge.description: One cubic Bézier segment from this node to the next (extension VTRY_curves, which a file using it lists in extensionsUsed and extensionsRequired). Its two control points, mm, in the piece frame.

line.description: An open path: nodes in order, each with the edge to the next one, except the last, which has none.

cut.description: One copy of the piece in the garment. mirrored: the mirror image (x -> -x in the piece frame), the other one of a left/right pair; references into it still use the piece's node ids and the piece frame's directions.

fabric.description: Overrides the garment's fabric for this cut.

appearance.description: Overrides the garment's appearance for this cut.

state.description: Absent: placed and draped. unplaced: waiting to be put on the body. set-aside: kept in the project, not draped. Either way the placement is a placeholder (format version 6).

layout.description: Where the cut sits in the 2D pattern view (mm, radians). Display only.

placement.description: Where the cut starts before sewing. wrap: rolled onto a cylinder around an avatar region. follow: on top of another cut (a pocket on a front), lifted off it.

region.description: wrap: a region name from the avatar's regions.

angle.description: Where the piece's centre goes around the axis, radians from the region's zero direction (follow: overrides the followed cut's).

top.description: wrap: position of the piece's top edge along the region's axis, mm from its origin (negative = down a limb).

rotation.description: In-plane rotation of the piece before wrapping, radians counter-clockwise (after mirroring).

tube.description: wrap: long sleeves. Below the piece's widest row the radius follows the pattern, tube x width / 2 pi (> 1 leaves a gap so the open edges meet under the arm); above it, it rises linearly to radius at the top edge.

offset.description: wrap: further out than the stack puts it, mm. Never negative; absent is 0.

cut.description: follow: the cut to follow (it must not itself follow this one, directly or not).

lift.description: follow: distance off the followed cut, mm.

run.description: A stretch of one cut's outline or internal line, between two of its nodes. On the outline, direction says which way round: ccw (the outline's order) or cw, in the piece frame (also for a mirrored cut). On an internal line, the run goes from 'from' to 'to' along the line.

line.description: Internal line id; absent = the outline.

seam.description: Two sides sewn together, each a chain of runs (a chain may span cuts). The start of a meets the start of b, the end of a the end of b.

pairing.description: nodes: if both sides pass through the same number of nodes, the nodes meet (notches line up) and each stretch in between is matched by length; otherwise as length. length: matched by length along the whole chain.

part.description: Path of the original file in the container, if kept.
